To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the conversion of vitamin A (retinal) to its biologically active form retinoic acid (retinal) is a developmentally regulated step involved in patterning of the dorso-ventral and antero-posterior axes of the Xenopus embryo.

retinol dehydratase 10 (RDH10) is a negative-feedback regulator of retinoxic acid signaling in the embryo, and that the combinatoric expression of RDH10 and retinal dehydrogeneses 2 (RALDH2) establishes a retinoxic acid morphogen gradient in Xenopus embryos.

the first enzyme in RA biosynthesis, retinol dehydratase 10, is a feedback regulator in RA signaling, which is important for the establishment and patterning of body axes and the central nervous system in Xenopus embryos.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of vitamin A and its derivatives in the development of vertebrates.
elucidation of the molecular mechanisms underlying the role of RA in early development of the vertebrate embryo.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms underlying the development of the vertebrate central nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RDH10 is a negative feedback regulator of retinoid signaling during axis formation and CNS pattern formation.
XRDH10 plays a role in RA synthesis during early development of Xenopus embryos.
RDH10 is a feedback-regulator of retinoic-acid signalling during axis formation, and patterning of Xenopus central nervous system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
XRDH10, a novel retinol dehyrogenase, is involved in the feedback regulation of RA signalling during Xenopus axis formation.

XRDH10, a novel enzyme that converts retinol into its active form retinal, is a feedback regulator in the RA signalling pathway and is essential for the establishment of RA gradients in Xenopus embryos.
XRDH10, a key enzyme for RA synthesis, is involved in the dorsoventrally patterned expression of XRALDH2 and in the regulation of RA signaling in the early Xenopus embryo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the biosynthetic enzyme code is a new paradigm to explain how a gradient of morphogen can be established in an embryo.
XRDH10, a novel member of the retinol dehydratase family, is a feedback regulator for RA signaling during axis formation and pattern formation of the central nervous systems.
the first step of retinol metabolism is also important for the development of the CNS.
